 Sporting CP and LASK Linz face off in round 3 of the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 league stage. The match takes place this Wednesday, 21 October 2026, at 20:00 (UK time) at the Estádio José Alvalade in Lisbon.
 Rui Borges’s rampant Portuguese champions return to continental action aiming to maintain their flawless European start, having swept aside Galatasaray (3-1) and Lens (2-0) while enjoying a weekend off to recharge their batteries. Across the pitch, Dietmar Kühbauer brings a LASK Linz side to the Portuguese capital that finally found domestic relief with a 4-0 league win on Saturday, but still carries the defensive scars of last week’s 6-3 demolition at the hands of Liverpool.
 This Sporting CP vs. LASK Linz prediction points toward a dominant, high-octane showing from the well-rested hosts under the Alvalade floodlights. Keep reading for our betting tips and analysis for this encounter, along with the probable line-ups.

 Sporting CP vs. Lask Linz - Head-to-head record
 The European history between these two sides features five competitive meetings, with the historical ledger perfectly balanced at two victories for Sporting CP, one draw, and two wins for LASK Linz.
 At the Estádio José Alvalade, Sporting have come out on top in two of their three previous home encounters against the Black-Whites, including a 4-0 victory in 1969 and a 2-1 Europa League win in 2019.
 However, LASK produced one of the most stunning results in their modern European history during their last visit to Lisbon in October 2020, running out 4-1 winners in a one-off Europa League play-off clash .
 Encounters between these clubs have always delivered entertainment for neutrals, with all five competitive meetings producing over 2.5 goals. With Sporting firing on all cylinders in attack and LASK struggling to contain top-tier European offenses, supporters can expect another high-scoring chapter in this fixture.

 Sporting CP - Enjoying an unbeaten streak
 Rui Borges’s side return to the Alvalade aiming to win their opening three Champions League matches for only the second time in club history. Below is an overview of the hosts’ current form, squad news, and projected starting XI:
 Recent form
 The Lions sit sixth in the 36-team Champions League standings on six points, carrying an impressive 10-match unbeaten streak across all competitions this season (seven wins and three draws) while plundering 25 goals in the process.
 Having sat out domestic action over the weekend, Borges’s men arrive thoroughly refreshed, and their home record in Europe is formidable: Sporting have won six of their last seven Champions League fixtures at the Alvalade.
 Colombian marksman Luis Javier Suárez will spearhead the frontline in scintillating form , having scored in each of his nine competitive starts this season to rack up 10 goals in all competitions, including two in Europe.
 Flanking Suárez in the final third will be Mozambique international Geny Catamo and dynamic Australian winger Nestory Irankunda, with Brazilian prospect Luis Guilherme (or Flávio Gonçalves) pulling the strings as the central playmaker.
 Borges must manage a few key absences, as midfielder Rodrigo Zalazar (muscle) and winger Nuno Santos (knee) remain sidelined alongside defender Zeno Debast.
 Summer arrival Issa Doumbia partners Sergi Altimira in the double pivot after scoring against Lens, while Brazilian shot-stopper Kaique Pereira guards the goal behind Iván Fresneda, Eduardo Quaresma, Gonçalo Inácio, and Maximiliano Araújo.

 Lask Linz - Bouncing back with a win
 Dietmar Kühbauer brings his LASK Linz squad to Lisbon looking to kickstart their maiden Champions League campaign following a confidence-restoring 4-0 domestic triumph over Austria Lustenau on Saturday. Here is an examination of the visitors’ tactical setup, squad updates, and expected starting lineup ahead of kickoff:
 Recent form
 The Black-Whites sit 33rd in the Champions League table with zero points, having opened with a frustrating 1-0 defeat at AEK Athens before being overwhelmed 6-3 by Liverpool in a nine-goal thriller.
 While LASK average 2.6 goals per game across all competitions this term , continental road trips have been an agonizing hurdle: the Austrian side have suffered nine consecutive away defeats in European competition, failing to score in seven of them.
 Towering forward Sasa Kalajdzic and Nigerian striker Samuel Adeniran will form a physical, direct strike partnership designed to test Sporting’s central defenders in the air.
 Wing-back Junior Yvan Dibango remains LASK’s primary creative catalyst after setting up all three goals against Liverpool.
 Kühbauer must contend with several injury doubts, with Moses Usor (shoulder), George Bello (muscle), and Ramiz Harakaté all facing late fitness checks. Melayro Bogarde and Alessandro Schöpf will anchor the engine room alongside Sascha Horvath, while Lukas Jungwirth starts in goal behind a back three of Xavier Mbuyamba, Alemão, and Andrés Andrade, flanked by Kasper Jørgensen on the right.

 Predictions for Sporting CP vs. Lask Linz - Home side to dominate
 Sporting CP have averaged 2.5 goals per match this season, while LASK Linz have conceded seven goals across their opening two Champions League outings. With the Portuguese hosts well-rested and LASK’s backline repeatedly exposed on their continental travels, backing Over 3.5 goals and the match not to end in a draw represents an enticing selection.
 Sporting rarely take time to find their rhythm at Alvalade. Driven by early strikes from Luis Suárez and Geny Catamo, Rui Borges’ side have broken the deadlock inside the opening half-hour in nine of their 10 matches this season. With LASK repeatedly caught cold before the interval in Europe, backing the Lions to lead at the break carries plenty of weight.
 While LASK can look to their shock 4-1 triumph in Lisbon six years ago for inspiration, this is an entirely different Sporting outfit. The Portuguese champions are purring in attack, rested, and operating on a different technical plane to an Austrian backline that shipped six to Liverpool. Back Sporting on the -1.5 Asian Handicap line to clear a two-goal margin.
